messages:
Maria (support): Hey team, customer in Berlin reporting suddenly hitting a US POP for inference requests since ~09:10 CET, latency spiking from ~60ms to 420-700ms and a few 401s. Billing alert also triggered. Can we triage?
Derek (network): Thanks Maria — any client IPs or example request IDs?
Maria (support): Sent a short repro from the tenant: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-XXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-small"}' --show-error
Response headers show: x-pop: us-east-1, x-request-id: rq_81b3f6, x-auth-status: 401 (intermittent). Customer IP: 82.184.21.34
Julia (sre): Ops-bot, run resolver path check for 82.184.21.34 and service domain.
ops-bot: automated-check: dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai returns 3 IPs: 18.201.34.12 (eu-west-1), 34.204.11.77 (us-east-1), 44.33.22.11 (eu-central-1). RTTs from our edge-probe near FRA: eu-central 12ms, eu-west 28ms, us-east 145ms. EDNS-client-subnet sent: 82.184.21.34 -> resolver responded with us-east 34.204.11.77. TTLs on answer: 300s
Derek (network): That looks like upstream resolver returning us-east for that EDNS payload. Could be ISP resolver mangling ECS or Cloudflare returning a suboptimal mapping. Which resolver did the customer use?
Maria (support): They say ISP's default DNS (posteo-net). Repro done from home / corporate — both show same.
Julia (sre): Two things to consider: 1) upstream resolver returning nonlocal A record (EDNS strip/misproxy) 2) our fallback policy might be selecting first compatible POP by IP order rather than preference by region latency. Need logs from the runtime routing decision for rq_81b3f6.
Derek (network): Maria, can you ask customer for a quick `dig +trace api.redwood.ai` and paste the full answer chain? Also ask them to test `dig @8.8.8.8 +short api.redwood.ai` and `dig @1.1.1.1 +short api.redwood.ai`
Maria (support): Done, customer pasted:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> @8.8.8.8 +short api.redwood.ai
34.204.11.77
18.201.34.12
44.33.22.11
```
From their corporate resolver (internal): returns only 34.204.11.77.
Derek (network): Ok ISP is returning only US IP. Likely EDNS-client-subnet is stripped/rewritten. That explains nonlocal pop. For the 401s: are the 401s always when routed to us-east?
Maria (support): Customer reports 401s only during the spike window, mostly when connecting to us-east addresses. They also saw token verification latency leading to timeout on retries (they retry with exponential backoff).
Julia (sre): Two immediate mitigation options: 1) Add a routing override for that tenant to prefer eu-central if client IP geolocates to DE (short-term). 2) Add a response-layer check to prefer lower-latency POP when multiple A records exist (we currently rely on resolver order). I'll check runtime logs for rq_81b3f6 and pattern around 09:10-09:25 CET.
ops-bot: runtime-log-scan: found 12 requests from 82.184.21.34 between 09:08-09:22 CET. Routing decisions: 9 routed -> us-east-1 (IP chosen 34.204.11.77), 3 routed -> eu-central-1. Reason code: resolver-preference. Auth service logs: token validation latency at us-east peaks 320ms causing some validation timeouts (threshold 250ms) => 401 returned.
Derek (network): Sounds like combined failure: ISP DNS causing wrong pop + auth validation slower cross-region due to unexpected load. Root cause: resolver answers. Action: open ISP probe with traceroute and ask customer to test a flush and alternative resolver (1.1.1.1).
Maria (support): Customer tested 1.1.1.1 and now gets eu-central IPs consistently and latency back to 55ms. They can't change their corporate resolver easily.
Julia (sre): Ok mitigation plan: I will create a tenant-scoped routing rule to pin that tenant to eu-central for 24 hours while we investigate. Derek, can you add a probe to detect when resolver answers nonlocal-only IPs for DE prefixes and trigger an alert?
Derek (network): On it — will add an automated check to compare EDNS-derived geo vs returned A-record geo and flag if mismatch rate > 30% in 10m window.
Maria (support): I'll notify customer of the temporary pin, and ask for any logs if it recurs. Also raising an internal ticket: INC-2026-4892 linking runtime logs and ops-bot output. :white_check_mark:
Julia (sre): Note for postmortem: consider improving routing policy to consult our own geolocation mapping when resolver responses are ambiguous, and add token validation circuit-breaker thresholds per region.
Derek (network): Agreed. Adding to network backlog.
Maria (support): Thanks all — I'll update the customer and close the loop after the pin window. :thumbsup:
